BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller material:** Counterparty draft – reviewed against Buyer Playbook. Nothing in the Seller's documents is treated as "agreed", "settled" or "cleared"; no Amelia Frost fallback authority has been given on any point.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback, but no written Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft exists, so it is not available to us.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure would strip AUD 250,000 from every recovery – no fallback exists for any of these.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims; limitations apply only to the category they are expressly drafted for.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the default-sweep language would quietly import general limits into Title/Tax/IP/indemnity claims (see N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap recovery on the one thing we are paying AUD 24m for – ownership of the shares.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – insert express carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and Schedule 7.** Non-negotiable under the playbook; no one on our side may waive it, and the absence of the carve-out in the Seller draft is itself a red flag.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only – facts disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: REJECT [1.1] and [1.2]; require a specific disclosure standard.** Whole-data-room disclosure would convert every unread document into a warranty defence and gut the warranty package. Note also [1.4] – the Seller's blanket non-admission – should not prevent the specific items in sections 2–10 being treated as disclosed *facts* for our risk allocation.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion. If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals (and warranties qualified by named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry), and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable from the data room" is constructive-knowledge language that, combined with N-006, would leave the Buyer with almost no enforceable warranty.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only; consent "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter s.2 confirms **no** final written consent and **no** evidence of satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion condition requiring (a) effective, unconditional Bluefen consent under cl 11.2 **and** (b) evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a ~30% revenue customer.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – redraft as a hard condition precedent with evidence requirement.** Consent-on-delivery would let a conditional or ineffective consent satisfy the CP while ~AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue remains exposed.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 facility addressed by a release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter s.3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark; direct repayment from Completion funds; executed security releases (incl. PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – require payout and releases at Completion as a Completion deliverable.** Buying a debt-free/cash-free company while the bank's security remains on foot after we have paid is a direct breach of the price basis; no Amelia Frost approval exists for the post-Completion route.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter s.5 confirms amounts are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals as applicable) as a specific funds-flow line item, either paid by Seller or deducted from the price as Transaction Expenses/Debt. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – insert express line item and Seller-funding mechanism; request on-cost quantification.** "A matter for the Seller" with no funds-flow entry means the Company (i.e., the Buyer post-Completion) ends up paying them.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). Disclosure Letter s.4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room; the AUD 180,000 is not bank-verified.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering (a) all loss from any defect in title to or ownership of SOW3 (and related) Project Materials, (b) any third-party IP claim by Ironquay, and (c) costs of securing a confirmatory assignment – while preserving the cure path (pay SOW3 fees and obtain assignment pre-Completion). The AUD 180,000 figure should not be treated as verified in either direction.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "adequate"; counter with broadened indemnity plus a pre-Completion cure deliverable (evidence of cleared payment + confirmatory assignment).** The risk is loss of IP ownership, not merely a AUD 180,000 payable, and the Seller's own disclosure confirms neither payment nor assignment is evidenced.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter s.6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown; investigation preliminary; no confirmed breach; no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide written updates and the final report; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (including any notification, regulatory or third-party exposure) if it crystallises; no acceptance of "not material" as a disclosure defence. Assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT "not material"; require investigation/update covenants and a bespoke indemnity, without asserting a breach.** Materiality cannot be assessed while the Seller's own disclosure says access, scope and notification are undetermined.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals, AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000), are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter s.8: DD-008/DD-011 to be read together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Fact-based assessment – timing, commitment status, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-paid or relates to pre-Completion periods – before deciding on any Debt/working-capital or price treatment. No automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT CONCEDE "ordinary course"; raise targeted DD questions and reserve position.** The Seller's label is an assertion unsupported by its own disclosure, but our playbook equally does not pre-judge the answer.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 13); limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax and IP folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, leakage, completion accounts) and covenant/indemnity claims each in their own regime; general caps/thresholds/time limits apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – reverse the default so limitations apply only where expressly stated and only to general Warranty Claims.** The Seller's drafting is a hidden general-regime override that would make N-004, N-011, N-012 and N-016 protections illusory.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter s.10 concedes this is the source relied on and does not state the Buyer has verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – current ASIC company extract and member search, PPSR searches against Company and Seller, certified board/shareholder resolutions and director authority evidence for Seller, original share certificates (or lost-certificate statutory declarations), and confirmation of no encumbrances, options or pre-emptive rights.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT DD-012 as sufficient; add independent title and authority evidence as Completion deliverables and keep Title warranties under the Fundamental regime.** A Company-maintained register is Seller-supplied internal material, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain **open**; Tax warranties/indemnity and IP warranties to sit in separate regimes with their own caps and periods (to be negotiated – no assumption of unlimited liability); nothing deemed settled by inclusion in the Seller's summary.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "settled" – respond that Tax and IP are expressly reserved and will be addressed by separate schedules.** Our playbook records these as unresolved; a counterparty asserting they are "settled" does not make them so.

---

## Summary table

| Ref | Issue | Seller position | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| N-001 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | Reject – 25% / 6.0m (no fallback authority) |
| N-002 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess-only | Reject – 5k / 50k / first-dollar |
| N-003 | Time limit | 18 months + "all Claims" sweep | Reject – 24 months; delete sweep |
| N-004 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Reject – 100% / 6 yrs / outside basket |
| N-005 | Fraud | No carve-out | Reject – insert, non-waivable |
| N-006 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Reject – specific fair disclosure |
| N-007 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Reject – delete cl 8.3 |
| N-008 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | Reject – hard CP + evidence of conditions |
| N-009 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Reject – payout + releases at Completion |
| N-010 | Bonuses | "Seller matter", not in funds flow | Reject – line item + on-costs, Seller-funded |
| N-011 | Ironquay | SOW3-only, "adequate" | Reject – broaden; preserve cure; verify 180k |
| N-012 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Don't accept; investigation covenants + indemnity; no breach assumed |
| N-013 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Don't concede; assess; no automatic Debt/price treatment |
| N-014 | Category separation | Default limits apply to all Claims | Reject – reverse default |
| N-015 | Title | DD-012 register | Don't accept; independent evidence |
| N-016 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | Reject – expressly open |

**Overall:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from a Buyer standpoint – every one of the 16 points is at or beyond the Seller-favourable end, and several (N-003/N-005/N-006/N-007/N-014) interlock to neutralise the warranty package as a whole. Nothing in the Seller's draft should be treated as agreed, and no fallback positions are available without written authority from Amelia Frost. Suggested next step: issue a full mark-up on these points together with a supplementary DD request list for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar.

- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering (a) all loss from any defect in title to or ownership of SOW3 (and related) Project Materials, (b) any third-party IP claim by Ironquay, and (c) costs of securing a confirmatory assignment – while preserving the cure path (pay SOW3 fees and obtain assignment pre-Completion). The AUD 180,000 figure should not be treated as verified in either direction.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "adequate"; counter with broadened indemnity plus a pre-Completion cure deliverable (evidence of cleared payment + confirmatory assignment).** The risk is loss of IP ownership, not merely a AUD 180,000 payable, and the Seller's own disclosure confirms neither payment nor assignment is evidenced.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter s.6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown; investigation preliminary; no confirmed breach; no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide written updates and the final report; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (including any notification, regulatory or third-party exposure) if it crystallises; no acceptance of "not material" as a disclosure defence. Assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT "not material"; require investigation/update covenants and a bespoke indemnity, without asserting a breach.** Materiality cannot be assessed while the Seller's own disclosure says access, scope and notification are undetermined.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals, AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000), are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter s.8: DD-008/DD-011 to be read together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Fact-based assessment – timing, commitment status, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-paid or relates to pre-Completion periods – before deciding on any Debt/working-capital or price treatment. No automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT CONCEDE "ordinary course"; raise targeted DD questions and reserve position.** The Seller's label is an assertion unsupported by its own disclosure, but our playbook equally does not pre-judge the answer.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 13); limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); Tax and IP folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, leakage, completion accounts) and covenant/indemnity claims each in their own regime; general caps/thresholds/time limits apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation: REJECT – reverse the default so limitations apply only where expressly stated and only to general Warranty Claims.** The Seller's drafting is a hidden general-regime override that would make N-004, N-011, N-012 and N-016 protections illusory.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register. Disclosure Letter s.10 concedes this is the source relied on and does not state the Buyer has verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – current ASIC company extract and member search, PPSR searches against Company and Seller, certified board/shareholder resolutions and director authority evidence for Seller, original share certificates (or lost-certificate statutory declarations), and confirmation of no encumbrances, options or pre-emptive rights.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT DD-012 as sufficient; add independent title and authority evidence as Completion deliverables and keep Title warranties under the Fundamental regime.** A Company-maintained register is Seller-supplied internal material, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain **open**; Tax warranties/indemnity and IP warranties to sit in separate regimes with their own caps and periods (to be negotiated – no assumption of unlimited liability); nothing deemed settled by inclusion in the Seller's summary.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "settled" – respond that Tax and IP are expressly reserved and will be addressed by separate schedules.** Our playbook records these as unresolved; a counterparty asserting they are "settled" does not make them so.
